rationale: Block 4 covers clinical presentations of nerve root vs cord compression and dermatomal distributions — the L4/L5/S1 trap is a high-yield identification point.
Block 5 covers the pathological basis including disc herniation levels and the SLR test — the below-knee pain reproduction criterion is a key examination trap.
Block 7 covers physical examination and investigations including cauda equina syndrome — this is a surgical emergency trap and must be assessed at the Analyze level.
Block 9 covers management including the clinical distinction between neurogenic and vascular claudication — a key differential diagnosis trap for the OR exam.
